original_text: Asexual Reproduction Strategies Vegetative reproduction is any form of asexual reproduction occurring in plants in which a new plant grows from a fragment of the parent plant or a specialized reproductive structure. Many plants naturally reproduce this way, but it can also be induced artificially. Plants can reproduce asexually with the use of: Stolons horizontal stems Rhizomes  underground stems Cutting, grafting, mound layering, & aerial layering are some commonnatural vegetative methods
explanation: Vegetative reproduction is a natural or artificially induced form of asexual reproduction in plants, where a new individual grows from a fragment of the parent plant or from a specialized vegetative structure rather than seeds or spores. Natural asexual structures include stolons (above-ground horizontal stems) and rhizomes (underground horizontal stems). Horticulturalists can artificially propagate plants using common vegetative methods such as cutting, grafting, mound layering, and aerial layering.

questions.exp: Vegetative reproduction is a form of asexual reproduction in which new plants develop from vegetative parts of the parent plant (like stems or leaves).

questions.q: Which of the following are specialized stem structures used by plants to propagate asexually?
questions.exp: Stolons (horizontal above-ground stems) and rhizomes (horizontal underground stems) are specialized stems used for vegetative reproduction.

questions.q: Which of the following is an artificial or horticultural vegetative propagation method listed in the text?
questions.exp: Grafting, cutting, mound layering, and aerial layering are listed as common vegetative propagation methods.
